chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who marries his male slave to his female slave, then it occurs to him to take her away from him with his own consent. Is that considered a divorce by the slave? He said: Yes, because the master's divorce is her divorce, so the slave has no divorce except with the permission of his master.

key_terms.بِإِذْنِ مَوْلَاهُ: With the permission of his master
key_terms.يُزَوِّجُ عَبْدَهُ أَمَتَهُ: Marries his male slave to his female slave

ai.seo_question: Does a master have the right to divorce his slaves' marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the fiqh of 'abd and ama marriage, establishing that the master holds the right of talaq (divorce) for his slaves, a ruling derived from the principle that the slave's legal agency is subordinate to the master's. Safwan ibn Yahya, a key narrator in the chain, transmits this from Abu Ibrahim (al-Imam al-Sadiq), highlighting the practical application of ownership rights in marital dissolution within the Shia jurisprudential tradition.
